Strategy bitcoin purchases shrink as buybacks take priority ahead of earnings
body: Saylor skips his Sunday bitcoin chart as Strategy heads into earningsStrategy chairman Michael Saylor did not share his usual Sunday bitcoin chart this week. Bitcoin watchers read that as a sign that Strategy (MSTR), the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, may have paused its buying. Saylor was active on X on Sunday: he described bitcoin as "the moat" in a reply to Jack Dorsey. But the chart that usually comes before a purchase announcement did not appear. A missing chart is a signal, not a confirmation. The company's Monday filing will settle the question, and its third-quarter results follow on Thursday. --- Earlier: Bitcoin buyers are fighting back, but sellers aren't finished. Here are the two prices swing traders should watch --- What is the 'orange dot chart'?For more than a year, Saylor has posted a snapshot of Strategy's bitcoin tracker to X almost every Sunday. The chart plots the value of the company's holdings over time, and each orange dot marks a purchase. The graphic has historically come before a Monday 8-K filing confirming that Strategy bought bitcoin the previous week. The caption changes each week, but the message is usually the same: more coins are coming. Over the past two weeks, Saylor captioned the chart with variations on finding room for more orange, and both posts were followed by purchase disclosures. The pattern is not a fixed rule.

title: Bitcoin buyers are fighting back, but sellers aren't finished. Here are the two prices swing traders should watch
body: Bitcoin is approaching an important decision point for swing traders. Sellers have demonstrated their strength, but buyers are showing signs of defending the $80,000 area. The latest investingLive tradeCompass maps two conditional scenarios: bullish above $80,860 and bearish below $79,870. The challenge is distinguishing a temporary rebound from a more durable recovery, or a brief dip from another significant breakdown. Bitcoin tradeCompass: The bullish and bearish levels The tradeCompass identifies two directional thresholds. Traders can use them to prepare for either outcome rather than commit to a prediction. Bullish Bitcoin above $80,860 A sustained move above $80,860 would strengthen the case that Bitcoin's recent stabilization is developing into a more meaningful recovery. The potential bullish profit targets are: The first target at $81,770 represents the initial opportunity to secure a partial profit. The higher targets provide objectives if buying momentum develops into a more substantial swing. Importantly, the bullish threshold has already been tested. On October 25, Binance BTC/USDC traded as high as approximately $80,942 before retreating below $80,860. A subsequent market snapshot around 20:04 UTC showed Bitcoin near $80,453. That brief crossing is not sufficient by itself to establish a confirmed breakout or an executed trade. Traders considering the bullish scenario should reassess whether price can regain and hold above the threshold.

title: Preview: RBNZ set to lift OCR to 3% ahead of election as oil and weak kiwi fuel inflation
body: With a hike close to fully priced, the New Zealand dollar's reaction is likely to hinge on guidance rather than the move itself, and the risk is asymmetric: a hold would catch markets badly offside and could trigger a sharp kiwi selloff. A hike paired with a clear tightening bias would be the most supportive outcome for the NZD and would push front-end yields higher, while "wait and see" language could see some of the priced peak trimmed. Oil remains the key external driver: further gains in crude linked to the Middle East conflict would feed straight into New Zealand's fuel-heavy inflation outlook and strengthen the case for more hikes into 2027. AUD/NZD traders also face back-to-back central bank risk, with the RBA expected to hike again on November 3. --- A pause looked likely in September, but rising fuel costs and a sliding kiwi have turned Wednesday's RBNZ meeting into a near-certain pre-election hike.

title: Weekend - China warns of countermeasures as US Treasury widens tech investment curbs to biotech
body: The proposal adds to already tense US-China relations and keeps headline risk elevated for Chinese technology and biotech stocks, including US-listed ADRs and the Hang Seng Tech index. Biotech is the sector most directly exposed, since it is the newly targeted industry and has relied more heavily on cross-border funding than areas already under restriction. Beijing has not named the countermeasures it might take, and that vagueness tends to keep investors cautious until the response becomes clear. A long public comment period leaves time for negotiation, but it also stretches the uncertainty out for months, which could weigh on risk appetite toward China-exposed assets and the offshore yuan if rhetoric escalates. -- Washington wants to stop US capital from funding China's next generation of strategic technology, and Beijing is signalling that it will not take the move quietly.

title: Goldman Sachs cuts Kospi target 25% to 9,000, still sees over 60% upside
body: The cut removes one of the most bullish institutional Kospi targets from the table, but the bank's insistence on deep value gives contrarian investors a framework for buying into weakness rather than chasing the selloff lower. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix remain the swing factor, since any stabilisation in sentiment toward AI capital spending would likely feed directly into the index given their weight. The sector preferences point to a possible rotation inside Korean equities, away from memory chips and toward power, industrials and domestically focused names, which could limit the downside for the broader market even if chip stocks stay under pressure. Foreign investor flows will be the key signal of whether the valuation argument is gaining traction. --- Goldman Sachs has blinked on its Kospi call but not folded, arguing that a market trading at about four times earnings is pricing in a chip downturn far worse than is likely.

title: RBA's Hunter says inflation job not done after four hikes, November rise in view
body: The comments should keep the Australian dollar supported, at the margin, on rate differentials and hold short-dated Australian government bond yields elevated, with markets likely to lean further toward a November hike unless Wednesday's inflation data surprise lower. Oil is the swing variable: renewed escalation in the US-Iran war that lifts crude would deepen the RBA's concern about second-round effects and raise the risk of tightening beyond November. A sustained easing in crude, by contrast, would give the board more room to signal a pause after its next move. Property-linked stocks and consumer discretionary names on the ASX remain exposed to a higher-for-longer policy path. - Earlier: Economic and event calendar in Asia Monday, October 26, 2026 - RBA speaker soon --- Four hikes in, the RBA's forecasting chief says the job is not finished, with war-driven oil costs working their way into supply chains and a fifth increase looking likely on November 3.
